title: Test Intent
description: [R3] A test written at story time, before the application exists. It says WHAT is being tested and WHAT must be observably true. It says nothing about where to click, because it cannot yet know. The binding phase of the Execution Agent (Agent 2a) binds an approved intent to a real page to produce a Test Mission, once per build and before any mission runs. See VISION sections 5a and 3.

test_id.description: Stable identifier, carried unchanged onto the mission the binding phase produces and onto every result. One id, one thread, requirement to defect.

requirement_ref.description: Traceability to the source requirement. Same shape as the mission's, so the binding phase copies it straight through.

locator.description: Path under input/feature*/, a ticket key, or a URL.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the captured requirement text, stamped at approval. Detects the requirement changing under an unchanged intent.

quote.description: The specific sentence(s) this intent is derived from.

depends_on_clarifications.description: [R3] Ids from input/feature*/clarifications.yaml that this intent's expected behaviour rests on. THE ENFORCEMENT HOOK: while any listed question is still 'open', Gate 2 refuses this intent. That is how 'never invent expected behaviour' stops being advice. A question answered as 'assumed' passes, but stamps assumption: true.

module.description: Optional at intent time. The module may not exist in knowledge/application-context.yaml yet, because it may not be built yet. The binding phase fills it in.

layer.description: The test case sheet's 'FE/BE?' column. FE: observed through the UI. BE: observed below it (API, job, data). FE+BE: needs both. Omitted, it is derived from coverage (api/integration → BE, otherwise FE).

capability.description: Dotted capability path, e.g. Auth.SignIn. A statement of product intent, not of UI.

browser.description: compatibility: the engine this test is about (webkit = Safari). Omit for Chromium. Usually better: run the whole suite with --browser instead of one intent per engine.

viewport.description: responsive: the screen size this test is about. Omit for desktop. One size per intent; a layout that must work on all three is three intents.

actor.description: Who is doing this, in product terms - 'Admin', 'an unauthenticated visitor', 'a user whose password has expired'. Deliberately NOT the mission's 'role' field, which must resolve against application-context.yaml. At intent time the role matrix may not be decided.

test_objective.description: One sentence. Neither the binding phase nor execution may alter it.

expected_outcome.description: 'blocked' means the application refusing the action is a PASS. Set here rather than at binding time, because it is a statement about the requirement, not about the UI.

preconditions.description: State that must hold before step 1, in business language: 'the account exists and is locked'. An unmet precondition is BLOCKED, never FAIL.

fault.description: error_handling: a backend failure this test simulates before the actor acts. Bound to a fail_requests step. The outcomes then say what the user must be told, and that nothing was lost or double-submitted.

endpoint.description: "POST /api/cart" when the requirement or documentation names it. Never invent one: without it a person picks the call at Gate 2.5.

description.description: The failure in product terms: "saving the cart fails on the server".

test_data.description: [R3] What STATE the data must be in, not which file to upload. Login is the case that proves why this belongs at intent time: half of a login suite needs accounts that are locked, expired, unverified or MFA-enrolled. Without somewhere to say so, those cases are generated, approved, and then turn out to be unrunnable - which looks exactly like the system failing.

description.description: The state required, e.g. 'a user account locked by 5 failed attempts'.

provisioning.description: 'unknown' is honest and useful: it lists, before anyone wastes a sprint, exactly which intents have no way to run yet.

disposable.description: True when the test consumes the account's usability - a lockout test poisons the account for every later run. Disposable data needs a fresh instance per run, not cleanup.

coverage.description: Which QA checklist area this covers. See agent/thinking/COVERAGE_CHECKLIST.md.

execution_mode.description: Best current guess. The binding phase may downgrade it to manual once it sees the real page; it may never upgrade it.

steps.description: [R3] What the actor does, in business language. There is deliberately no action enum, no target, no selector - not because the author should be careful, but because the schema cannot express one. The failure mode is designed out rather than warned about.

actor_intent.description: One thing the actor does: 'submit credentials for an account that is locked'. If you cannot write it without naming a button, it is a binding detail and belongs to the binding phase.

note.description: Anything the binding phase or a human reviewer needs to know about this step.

simulate.description: Something that happens TO the user at this point: session_expired ends the session as a timeout would. The next steps and outcomes say what the application must do about it.

api.description: A step done through the API instead of the UI: setting data up, or reading a record back to prove it was stored. Use only when the requirement or documentation names the endpoint.

endpoint.description: "POST /api/orders". {name} path parameters are filled from values saved by earlier steps.

outcomes.description: [R3] What must be observably true afterwards. The binding phase turns each of these into a mission assertion with a machine-checkable check; until then it stays a claim about the product, not about the DOM.

statement.description: The human sentence. This is what the reviewer - possibly the BA who wrote the story - reads at Gate 2.

observable.description: What KIND of evidence would settle this. The one concession to the executing side: enough for the binding phase to know which family of check to bind, while still saying nothing about the UI.

critical.description: Defaults to true. A non-critical outcome failing degrades the result to INCONCLUSIVE rather than FAIL.

not_verifiable_yet.description: [R3] Things this intent SHOULD check but currently cannot - no API client, no database access, no visual comparison, no second role. Written down here so the hole is scheduled rather than forgotten. Silence is not the same as 'fully covered', and an unstated gap is how a suite comes to look more complete than it is.

assumption.description: [R3] Stamped at approval when any depended-on clarification was answered 'assumed' rather than confirmed. It rides through the mission into the run report, so nobody mistakes a guess for an agreed requirement when the result comes back.

approval.description: Gate 2, made machine-checkable. The binding phase refuses any intent outside intents/approved/ or with this block absent.

edits_made.description: Did the human change the generated intent? Feeds the edit rate in docs/BASELINE.md.

review_minutes.description: The point of the intent/mission split is that this number should be SMALLER than the R2 mission review time. If it is not, the split is not paying for itself.

clarification_hashes.description: Q-id to sha256 of the answer text as it read at approval. If an answer is later revised and the intent is not, the intent is flagged stale instead of quietly testing a rule nobody agreed to any more.
